items.title: Cavaliers Sign Zack Austin To Two-Way Contract
items.summary: The Cavaliers continue to shuffle players in and out of their two-way contract slots, announcing today in a press release that they’ve signed swingman Zack Austin to a two-way deal. In order to make room for Austin, Cleveland placed forward Riley Minix on waivers. Austin, 25, is a 6’5″ wing who went undrafted out of Pitt in 2025. He was in camp with the Thunder in 2025 before spending his rookie year with their G League affiliate, the Oklahoma City Blue. In 20 games for the Blue, he averaged 12.9 points, 3.9 rebounds, and 2.2 blocks in 27.4 minutes per contest. Those block numbers weren’t an anomaly for Austin, who averaged 1.8 BPG during his college career and led the ACC in blocked shots as a senior. items.title: NBA Europe Likely Aiming For ‘Soft Launch’ Next Fall
items.summary: The NBA’s aim to start a European league next fall could be a “soft launch” at best, considering the league doesn’t have any teams yet, The Athletic’s Joe Vardon reports. The NBA has partnered with FIBA as it looks to establish its own European league, tentatively known as NBA Europe. “Broadly speaking, it is implausible that a serious league could be launched (by next October),” a member of one potential NBA Europe franchise ownership group told Vardon. NBA commissioner Adam Silver expressed confidence last month that the new league would move forward, even though negotiations with the existing EuroLeague hit a snag. There’s still no clear resolution, according to Vardon, nor are there any formal agreements in place with the soccer conglomerates, private equity chiefs, and tech giants needed to form new teams in Europe’s largest markets.
